messages.content: 你能使用 get_stock_prices 函數來檢索蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價嗎？。

function.name: get_stock_prices
function.description: Retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

companies.description: List of companies to retrieve stock prices for.

duration.description: Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc.

The function signature expects companies: string[], duration: string. But we need to call it multiple times? The user says "retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration". They want separate durations for each company? Actually they say "for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Tesla respectively in 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks and 1 month time ranges." That implies mapping: Apple -> 1 week, Microsoft -> 2 weeks, Amazon -> 3 weeks, Tesla -> 1 month. So we need to call get_stock_prices four times with single company each and respective duration.

We should produce calls to the function. According to guidelines, we can only output one function call at a time. We need to decide which order. Probably start with Apple 1 week. But the user explicitly asked to retrieve all. We could interpret that as making multiple calls. But guidelines: "When you do want to call a function, you must do so in a single assistant message. You may not provide additional text besides the function call." So we can only output one function call. But we can choose to call with all companies and maybe specify duration as array? But function expects duration string. So we can't pass array. So we need to call multiple times. But we can't output multiple calls. So we need to ask clarifying question? Or we can output the first call and then wait for the tool's response. But the user wants all data. We can comply partially: call for Apple 1 week. Then after receiving result, call for Microsoft 2 weeks, etc. But we need to handle this stepwise. So we will call for Apple 1 week first.
